item.title: Build memory-aware AI agents with Agentic Retrieve on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
item.description: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory now store conversations, extract facts, and bring long-term memory into a single AgenticRetrieveStream call. This post shows how to build a memory-aware, multi-user assistant where each user sees only the documents they may read and each user's memory stays private. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/build-memory-aware-ai-agents-with-agentic-retrieve-on-amazon-bedrock-managed-knowledge-base

item.title: How Duco transforms financial data automation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Duco, a data automation platform for tier-one banks, rebuilt its agentic AI stack on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. With strict per-tenant isolation, a multi-model strategy, and an MCP skills architecture that cut context overhead by 90%, Duco cut reconciliation deployment time 10x and onboarding costs 70%. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/how-duco-transforms-financial-data-automation-with-amazon-bedrock-agentcore

item.title: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing
item.description: Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem, not a model problem. This post gives a field-tested taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns and anti-patterns, a framework for deciding when multiple agents are warranted, and how to build cost-efficient, reliable systems on AWS. Worth a read for developers following AI and Architecture. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/taxonomy-of-multi-agent-design-patterns-anti-patterns-and-lessons-from-manufacturing

item.title: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: MoEngage built Merlin AI, a set of AI agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that let marketing and product teams draft, analyze, and adjust campaigns from a single conversation. Learn how MoEngage turned its existing APIs into MCP tools and kept each tenant's data isolated while giving agents secure access to live platform data. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/how-moengage-built-agentic-customer-engagement-on-amazon-bedrock-agentcore

item.title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform
item.description: Legacy mainframe Assembler applications are costly to maintain and hard to staff. This post presents a multi-stage, AI-powered methodology using Amazon Bedrock, Kiro IDE, and AWS Transform to extract business rules, convert Assembler through an intermediate COBOL stage, and deploy modernized Java Spring Boot applications on AWS. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/modernizing-mainframe-assembler-to-java-using-amazon-bedrock-and-aws-transform

item.title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
item.description: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so agentic retrieval can answer questions over CSV, XLSX, and XLS files. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/get-answers-from-tables-with-tabular-search-in-amazon-bedrock-managed-knowledge-base

item.title: Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
item.description: With Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, you block a content category by describing it in plain language, and the guardrail matches by meaning rather than keyword, which can block more than you intend. This post presents eight best practices for writing a topic precisely enough that the guardrail blocks what you mean and passes what you don't. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.

item.title: Customize answers per tenant in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

This post shows how to give each tenant its own answers, keep tenant data apart with metadata filters, scope access with IAM tags, and roll out changes one tenant at a time. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/customize-answers-per-tenant-in-amazon-bedrock-managed-knowledge-base

item.title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Many generative AI applications resend the same long context on every request. Prompt caching lets open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock reuse it to reduce input cost and latency. This post shows implicit and explicit caching through the Chat Completions API and applies caching to an OpenCode coding agent session. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/use-prompt-caching-with-open-weight-models-on-amazon-bedrock

item.title: Worse is better: async/await versus syntactic sugar for monadic composition
item.description: A missed opportunity masquerading as a killer feature. In this article, I will argue that the celebrated async / await language feature pioneered by C# should rather be classified as a missed opportunity. F# did async first, and better,…

item.title: Database Performance: Up to 11× Faster Workloads with Connection Pooling
item.description: Connection pooling significantly enhances database operation efficiency by reusing existing connections, reducing setup time. In SQLite benchmarks, pooling achieved up to an 11× speedup under heavy concurrency. While beneficial for applications with frequent connections, pooling should be enabled by default, with exceptions for specific cases requiring immediate connection release. Worth a read for developers following Data and .NET. Link to article: https://dotnettips.com/2026/11/15/database-performance-up-to-11x-faster-workloads-with-connection-pooling

item.description: Coding agents work in tasks, and the number that matters is cost per solved task, not price per token. In this post, you use the AWS CDK to deploy LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin on Amazon Bedrock, then measure cost per solved task for a routed model group against single-model baselines. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. item.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
item.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots your initialized environment and restores it for each new session, so session start no longer grows with image size. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and four patterns to keep work off the first request. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/architecture-patterns-for-fast-session-startup-on-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-runtime

The post covers asynchronous inference, multi-GPU parallelism, bringing your own MSAs for accuracy and privacy, and scaling to zero to reduce cost. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. C# 15 and .NET 11 shipped … Continue reading C# 15 Labeled Break Continue The post C# 15 Labeled Break Continue appeared first on NDepend Blog .

item.description: November 13, 2026 9 minutes read A C# closed class is a class whose direct subclasses all live in its own assembly. The closed modifier, new in C# 15, tells the compiler that this set of subclasses is complete. As a result, a switch expression that handles each subclass needs no default arm.
